summary: Intermittent p99 throughput collapse in dedicated pool correlated with one tenant's high-churn small requests
description:
Issue summary: Customer Ledgerly AI reported recurring drops in throughput (p50 stable, p99 spiking to timeouts) on their dedicated pool during the morning traffic window. Impact: Several inference routes experienced elevated latency and streaming disconnects for ~10-30 minute windows. Environment: Dedicated pool in us-east-1, pinned model redwood/open-7b, autoscaler configured with burst-reservations enabled and per-tenant soft limits.

Observed behavior: p50 token latency normal, p99 token latency jumps from ~120ms to >2s; request success rate for streaming sessions fell to 85% for affected routes. No single host CPU/GPU fully saturated in metrics; however per-GPU kernel queues showed large variance and frequent small-kernel launch spikes.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer traffic pattern: dozens of concurrent clients issuing short (5-20 token) requests at high QPS from a single tenant ID.
2) Autoscaler set to conservative scale-up threshold; burst reservations allowed but limited to pool-wide quota.
3) Observe serving-runtime telemetry: rapid kernel churn and KV cache thrashing when many short sessions interleave on same GPUs.
4) Result: throughput collapse at p99 and intermittent streaming disconnects while p50 remains acceptable.
investigation:
Initial triage (Support): gathered request traces, customer-side load pattern, and timestamps. Correlated drops to 08:15-08:40 UTC window. SRE review: GPU utilization per-card moderate (40-60%) but scheduler queue lengths and kernel launch rate spikes aligned with incidents. Autoscaler logs showed repeated 'scale blocked by burst-reservation-quota' events. Hypothesis: a single tenant creating many short-lived sessions drives high kernel launch overhead and KV cache churn; autoscaler did not scale fast enough because burst reservations exhausted pool allowance and scale-up cooldowns preserved capacity but allowed latency to degrade.

Instrumentation used: per-tenant request histogram, kernel-launch-rate metric, KV cache hit/miss ratio, autoscaler decision trace. Dashboards referenced: #ops/dedicated-pools, Serving Runtime per-GPU kernel telemetry. Linked Slack: https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C0123456/p1678200000000
logs:
Example error lines from serving runtime at 2026-03-08T08:19:31Z: 
[serving-runtime][WARN] kernel_launch_rate=1342/s gpu_card=card-7 queue_len=27 tenant_id=ledgerly session_id=xyz123
[autoscaler][INFO] scale-up blocked reason=burst_quota_exhausted pool=dedicated-56 available_burst=0
[api-gateway][ERROR] stream_disconnected session=abc789 reason=upstream-timeout status=504

Attached traces: trace ids: trc-20260308-081931-az1, trc-20260308-082100-az2
diagnosis: Root cause: workload coupling between tenant-level request fanout and kernel-level execution cost. Short request patterns cause high per-request kernel overhead and KV cache churn; this increases effective per-token cost and reduces realized throughput at tail latencies. Autoscaler configuration allowed pool-level burst reservations that were consumed quickly by the tenant, preventing timely scale-up. No single GPU reached thermal or power limits; problem is scheduling inefficiency + autoscale policy interaction (burst quota + cooldown).
resolution:
Applied a multi-step mitigation and fix: 
1) Immediate (hotfix) - applied per-tenant request concurrency cap and short-request soft-rate-limit for Ledgerly AI to reduce kernel churn (rolled out 2026-03-08T09:10Z).
2) Short-term SRE action - temporarily increased pool burst-reservation quota and decreased autoscaler cooldown to allow faster scale-up during bursts (rolled out 2026-03-08T09:35Z).
3) Serving runtime change - enabled small-request batching window (20ms) for the affected routes to reduce kernel launch overhead (deployed 2026-03-11 via PR 768).
4) Follow-up - created autoscale policy change to account for kernel_launch_rate as a first-class signal; plan tracked in INT-9021.

Result: p99 token latency returned to baseline within 20 minutes of hotfix; streaming disconnect rate returned to <1%. Customer confirmed service quality improved and accepted temporary rate caps while fix rolled out.
postmortem_notes:
Action items: 
- Engineering: implement kernel_launch_rate-based autoscaler signal (INT-9021).
- Product: document recommended request sizing guidance for dedicated customers (confluence page created).
- Support: add automated alert when per-tenant kernel_launch_rate exceeds threshold.

Lessons learned: autoscaler should consider workload shape (many short sessions) not just aggregate GPU utilization. Dedicated pools require per-tenant fairness controls to avoid noisy-neighbor scenarios. Batching heuristics for short requests materially reduce overhead.
resolution_status: Workaround applied and runtime change deployed; long-term autoscaler change in progress (INT-9021). Customer uplifted and monitoring alerts added to the pool dashboard.
